This chapter introduces a foundational approach to integrating social media sentiment with traditional statistical models for predicting football outcomes. It establishes a methodological framework where tweet data is processed through a bag-of-words representation, filtered by part-of-speech tags and ranked using chi-square and mutual information metrics. These features are then fed into various machine learning classifiers—Naive Bayes, Random Forests, Logistic Regression, and SVM—to assess their predictive power against historical match statistics. The core insight lies in demonstrating that social media signals can offer orthogonal information beyond conventional team performance indicators. This supports the development of GSI's Bayesian inference engines by providing a structured way to incorporate external textual data into probabilistic models. For GSE, it offers a principled mechanism to encode situational awareness through dynamic sentiment vectors that evolve with real-time engagement, enabling more adaptive tactical reasoning. The paper's emphasis on i.i.d. assumptions and fixed pre-match windows aligns with GSE's need for temporal consistency in state transitions, while its reliance on specific APIs and datasets underscores the importance of data governance and reproducibility in scalable systems.
